One of every four decoder layers in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next utilizes Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) rather than linear attention, pairing full self-attention expressive power with an MQA micro-block indexer to bound sequence compute within an active token budget. Implementing QSA requires partial interleaved multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (mRoPE), key-pooled micro-block indexing returning selected block indices, and gated query-output projection aligned with reference PyTorch semantics.

Every decoder layer in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next utilizes a 512-expert Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) block with top-10 softmax routing and 1 scalar-gated shared expert, providing 180B total parameter capacity with bounded active compute per token. Implementing this architecture requires 3D-stacked routed expert parameters, vectorized gather/einsum dispatch, float32 router probabilities with top-k sum normalization, and scalar-gated shared expert combination aligned with reference PyTorch semantics.
Implement SplitMix64 n-gram hashing and Layer-2 PLE module.

Assembling the complete Qwen3.8-Flash-Next architecture requires integrating the 4-stream Hyper-Connection residual structure, heterogeneous 4-layer cycle blocks (3 GDN linear attention layers + 1 QSA sparse attention layer), Layer-2 Pre-Layer Embedding (PLE), and 512-expert Sparse MoE feed-forward blocks into an end-to-end model with both unrolled and scan-compatible execution modes.

Training Qwen3.8-Flash-Next requires Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) draft modeling and joint loss evaluation across primary autoregressive cross-entropy, MoE router load-balancing, and shifted next-token MTP predictions.
